_why: A scoring tool is a hypothesis until it agrees with cases a human labelled by hand. Every entry here is a skill someone READ and judged. If the scorer disagrees with a label, the SCORER is presumed wrong, not the label. Run: python3 scripts/skill_quality.py --self-test
_history: 08-08-2026: v1 of this scorer gave pr-pitch-writer 35/100 because its author allowlist had never met 'Holiday' and its self-check regex only matched ## headings. Acting on that score would have damaged good skills. These fixtures exist so that failure mode fails the tool instead of the skills.

09-08-2026: retro was remediated (evidence tiers, write gate, evals) and rose 55 -> 95. Its 'weak' label was true of the OLD artifact and is now stale, so it is re-labelled. A fixture that is never updated becomes a lie about the present.

09-08-2026: the rubric was found to score UNMIGRATED skills (no metadata.grounded_in) at ~3/100, e.g. confluence-to-md at 294 lines. A scope guard now excludes them rather than emitting a meaningless number.
